epic.title: compat(webContents): navigation event vocabulary, navigation policy, window-open handler, executeJavaScript, preload registration, print/devtools
epic.body:
## Scope
34 entities / 381 members: `WebContents` (195), `WebFrameMain`, `NavigationHistory`, `Debugger`, `webFrame` (renderer), `webContents` module, input-event and print structures, `sharedTexture`/offscreen structures (never). Live today: no WebContents facade; keld-wv `WebEngine` = create/navigate/eval(fire-and-forget)/bounds/devtools/destroy; the only navigation observable is a page-load-finished event; Windows denies popups and guards permission requests; the KEL-142 macOS bridge supplies the isolated-world injection seam and a navigation generation counter.

## Corpus demand (resolved)
`will-navigate` + unconditional `preventDefault` and `setWindowOpenHandler` (both apps; Zettlr deny-all, draw.io allows only `about:blank` with `overrideBrowserWindowOptions` after an `openExternal` side effect); `webContents.send` (Zettlr 49 / draw.io 9); `did-finish-load`; `loadURL`/`loadFile`; awaited `executeJavaScript` (draw.io 5+); zoom; `printToPDF`/`print`; `openDevTools`; `render-process-gone`; `destroyed`; `before-input-event` + `pasteAndMatchStyle` (draw.io). Zero demand for NavigationHistory, Debugger, offscreen (except draw.io's export window), sharedTexture, WebFrameMain frame-tree APIs.

## Maturity ladder
- L0: `webContents` facade exists with typed errors; never-list rows published.
- L1: `loadURL/loadFile`, `did-finish-load`, `send`, `executeJavaScript` work for quick-start and draw.io on macOS.
- L2: ordered navigation vocabulary, will-navigate veto semantics (guard ∧ app), window-open handler default, destroyed semantics pass pinned conformance entries on each engine or carry an explicit per-engine ▲.
- L3: corpus apps' navigation workflows pass under `keld dev`.

## Linear owners consumed
KEL-79 (origin/resource/navigation/popup policy), KEL-132 (media/GPU), KEL-142 (isolated world, generation counter), KEL-135 (profile), KEL-80 (bounded host→renderer delivery), SCV codec owner (open — see F03-D4).

## Design facts fixed by research (two refuters)
- Split ownership: keld-wv delivers a small engine-neutral navigation signal set (provisional-start, commit, same-document change, dom-content-loaded, finish, fail{code}) per backend; Electron's event vocabulary is synthesised once above it (facade/keld-compat), keyed by `(WebviewId, navigation generation)`. One generation owner is required (two counters exist today: bridge vs guard) — decision F04-A4.
- Navigation policy is guard-first, app-hook deny-only: the app's `will-navigate`/`will-frame-navigate` hook is invoked for every page-initiated cross-document navigation, the guard decision is computed independently, outcome = guard ∧ app; programmatic `loadURL` bypasses the app hook but not the guard.
- `setWindowOpenHandler`: the handler is always invoked (draw.io's has side effects); unrecognised returns are deny; default without handler is deny-with-diagnostic (▲ or `windowOpenHandler` quirk, chosen in the PR); `allow` requires synchronous host window minting inside the engine delegate.
- `executeJavaScript` needs an `EvalCallback` result envelope on `WebEngine::eval` and a structured-clone-compatible codec; the SCV codec has no owner yet (F03-D4 open).
- Preload runs in a dedicated app content world (third world), not the trusted KEL-142 world — panel contested decision; F07 owns the preload runtime.
- Devtools are dev-only; a host print broker serves `printToPDF`/`print`; `Debugger` is ✘.

'Entries may fail (red) until the implementing tickets land; they must not be skipped or retried' collides with the verification floor (reported passing workspace tests; merge admission enforced — KEL-128 Done) and with 'MUST NOT weaken tests / skip gates'. No mechanism is named that lets a red entry coexist with a green required gate.

refuter_verdicts_batch1.lens: Keld invariants, ownership and reuse: four uniques; default-deny never bypassed; no Electron-isms in host crates outside keld-compat/@keld/electron; one owner per policy/schema/parser/lifecycle state; reuse of KEL-75/79/80/102/135/142 owners; spec+Linear gate; prior decisions #312/#313/#319/#322/#323/#325 and KEL-127. Verified against <keld repo> at d150a14 (arch 01-05, keld-wv engine.rs / wkwebview/mod.rs / macos_bridge.rs / webview2/mod.rs, keld-guard lib.rs, specs kel102/kel142/kel75/kel98, research 186/195/214/13, incubator 16b/16c/16d, learnings, compat-scoreboard) plus Linear KEL-79 retrieved live 2026-10-06.

verdicts.reason: The identity atoms survive (webContents.id = host WebviewId; promise correlation per generation; raw engine signals per backend), but the ownership atom is wrong on two counts. (1) Placing a state machine in keld-wv that 'synthesizes Electron's event vocabulary' and emits 'a pinned-oracle ordered sequence' puts an Electron-ism (Electron's event names and total order) into the engine crate, whereas arch 04 §3 layer 4 assigns host-side emulation of 'webContents routing identity' to the keld-compat crate and keld-compat/AGENTS.md says compat pressure stays there; arch 05 §1 describes keld-wv's job as generic hooks ('principal identity per navigation, pre-load script atomicity, navigation interception, window.open handling, print, zoom, find'), not Electron ordering. (2) 'Reusing KEL-142's generation counter as the single document-identity source' names the wrong owner: KEL-102 §(GuardSnapshot) says the Webview principal generation is 'Created and rotated only by the host webview/navigation registry' and arch 03 §1 says webview identity 'is derived from the host's engine/navigation registry'; the bridge's BridgeState.navigation_generation (macos_bridge.rs:301,334) is a private per-bridge counter bumped from wry PageLoadEvent::Started (wkwebview/mod.rs page_load_trace_handler) while the guard principal generation is still 0 (arch 03 §4.3). Today there are two counters and no registry; the destination owner is the keld-core registry (arch 01 §3 table: keld-core owns 'window registry'), which engine.rs's module doc also names as the owner of the callback/command-queue plumbing. Minor: the quoted sentence 'principal generation rotates; pending replies to the old principal drop' is arch 02 §7 line 362, not §5.
verdicts.evidence: docs/architecture/04-electron-compat.md §3 item 4 ('Host-side emulation (keld-compat crate) ... webContents routing identity'); crates/keld-compat/AGENTS.md ('compat pressure stays here'); docs/architecture/05-webview-and-native.md §1 'Why not just use wry' (a)/(b); crates/keld-wv/src/engine.rs module doc ('the callback plumbing belongs to the command-queue design keld-core will own'); docs/specs/kel102-host-guard-enforcement.md TrustedCaller::Webview comment + 'a later navigation registry must increment it'; docs/architecture/03 §1 lines 28-30; crates/keld-wv/src/wkwebview/macos_bridge.rs:301-336; crates/keld-wv/src/wkwebview/mod.rs:693-704; docs/architecture/02-ipc.md:362.
verdicts.correction: Split the machine: keld-wv HostHooks (design review, arch 05 §1 sketch) delivers a small engine-neutral navigation signal set — provisional-start, commit, same-document-change, dom-content-loaded, finish, fail{engine code}, title-change, content-process-terminated — each tagged with (WebviewId, generation) that the host navigation registry mints (keld-core owner per arch 01 §3 / KEL-102; the KEL-142 bridge and the guard principal both consume that one counter, replacing the private BridgeState counter). The Electron vocabulary, the did-* total order from the pinned oracle, loadURL promise settlement and WebFrameMain identity are synthesized once in keld-compat (host side) or @keld/electron, where keld-compat/AGENTS.md's ordering tests apply. Cite arch 02 §7 for the rotation rule.

verdicts.reason: Guard-first, deny-only app hook, host-initiated loads bypass will-navigate but not the guard, failure before commit — all consistent with the repo contracts, and the engine pre-commit vetoes are corroborated by repo research (16b M8 decidePolicyForNavigationAction; 16c NavigationStarting; 16d PSON/decide-policy). research.summary: [fact] The family is 34 entities / 381 members (WebContents alone 195). Corpus demand is narrow and consistent: both draw.io Desktop and Zettlr register `will-navigate` with an unconditional `event.preventDefault()` plus a `setWindowOpenHandler` (Zettlr deny-all; draw.io allows only `about:blank` with `overrideBrowserWindowOptions`), rely on `webContents.send` (49 / 9 call sites), `did-finish-load` (draw.io 7), `loadURL`/`loadFile`, `executeJavaScript` with awaited results (draw.io 5), zoom (`zoomFactor`/`zoomLevel`/`setVisualZoomLevelLimits`), `printToPDF`/`print`, `openDevTools`/`toggleDevTools`, `render-process-gone`, `destroyed`/`did-navigate`/`isDestroyed`, `console-message`, `unresponsive`; no corpus app uses NavigationHistory, Debugger, offscreen, sharedTexture, WebFrameMain frame-tree APIs, or `<webview>` (draw.io's 7 hits all DISABLE it). [fact] Keld today has no WebContents facade at all: keld-wv v0 `WebEngine` = create/navigate/eval(fire-and-forget)/set_bounds/devtools(Open|Close)/destroy; the only navigation observable is `AppWindowEvent::NavigationReady` from wry `PageLoadEvent::Finished`; the only policy hooks are Windows deny-all `NewWindowRequested` + guarded `PermissionRequested` (type-witnessed before first navigation); the KEL-142 macOS bridge supplies the reusable pieces (isolated `WKContentWorld` document-start user scripts, host-owned navigation generation counter, pending-call invalidation on navigation, `KELD-WV-011`). Window registry (H7) is TARGET in keld-core; KEL-79 (origin/resource/navigation/popup policy) is Backlog; KEL-132 is In Progress. Design answer: implement this family ONCE as (a) one engine-neutral per-webview navigation state machine in keld-wv keyed by (WebviewId, navigation generation) that synthesizes Electron's event vocabulary from raw engine signals, (b) guard-first navigation/popup policy (default-deny, app hooks can only further deny; host-initiated loads bypass `will-navigate` exactly as Electron documents but never bypass the guard), (c) `eval` extended with a structured result envelope, (d) preload = host-injected isolated-world document-start script with the Electron sandbox `require` subset, (e) a serialized host print/PDF broker, (f) devtools off in release unless `web.devtools`. Documented divergences (▲): default window.open = deny, devtools default off in release, zoom per-view not per-origin, `render-process-gone.exitCode`/`unresponsive` absent on WKWebView, NavigationHistory `pageState`/`restore` ✘. Never: sharedTexture/offscreen, Debugger CDP in production, device emulation, WebRTC policy knobs, `clone()`, Node-in-webview (`sandbox:false` honoring), trusting invalid certs via `certificate-error`.

decisions.question: Where is Electron's navigation event vocabulary (did-start-loading … did-finish-load/did-fail-load, did-navigate(-in-page), dom-ready, will-redirect, page-title-updated, destroyed) produced, and from what identity?

decisions.question: Who decides whether a navigation proceeds, and what does `will-navigate` + `event.preventDefault()` mean under default-deny?
decisions.proposed_answer: Guard first, app second, deny-only hooks. The host evaluates every top-level/frame navigation against a generated allow-list (`web.navigate`-shaped origin/scheme scopes; app bundle resources and the app's own origin are implicit) BEFORE the engine commits (WK decidePolicyFor → .cancel/.allow; WebView2 NavigationStarting.Cancel; WebKitGTK decide-policy ignore/use). Only guard-allowed, non-host-initiated, non-same-document navigations are surfaced as `will-navigate`/`will-frame-navigate`, where the app may further deny; it can never widen. Host-initiated `loadURL`/`loadFile`/`reload`/`navigationHistory.go*` bypass `will-navigate` exactly as Electron documents but still pass the guard. Denied navigations produce a stable KELD code + diagnostic, not silence. Default allow-list scope is a user-owned choice (see unknowns).
evidence: [fact] Electron: 'This event will not emit when the navigation is started programmatically with APIs like webContents.loadURL and webContents.back. It is also not emitted for in-page navigations' (receipt R5).

decisions.question: What does `setWindowOpenHandler` do in Keld when the host cannot yet mint windows, and what is the default when no handler is registered?
decisions.proposed_answer: Default = deny with a diagnostic (documented ▲ against Electron's default of creating a BrowserWindow). `{action:'deny'}` and malformed returns are exact matches (Electron also treats unrecognized returns as deny). `{action:'allow'}` requires the host to synchronously mint a child window + webview inside the engine's delegate on the UI thread, with the engine-supplied configuration (WK) / related-view (WebKitGTK) / NewWindow target (WebView2), and inherit the opener's isolated world + preload + guard install — this is gated on the keld-core window registry (H7) and is Tier 2 for `about:blank` children (draw.io) with `overrideBrowserWindowOptions` validated against the profile (nodeIntegration:true never). `did-create-window` fires only on a host-minted child; `outlivesOpener:false` is enforced by window-generation revocation (arch 02 §5 window close). `window.open()` in the page must return `null` on deny (native semantics).
evidence: [fact] Electron: unrecognized return 'will result in a console error and have the same effect as returning {action: "deny"}'; handler is 'Called before creating a window when a new window is requested by the renderer, e.g. by window.open(), a link with target="_blank", shift+clicking on a link, or submitting a form with <form target="_blank">' (R6); `did-create-window` 'Not emitted if the creation of the window is canceled' (R7); 'By default, child windows are closed when their opener is closed' (R8); window.open 'Returns Window | null' and 'When opening about:blank, the child window's WebPreferences will be copied' (R9).

[fact] Corpus: Zettlr returns `{action:'deny'}` always; draw.io allows `about:blank` with `overrideBrowserWindowOptions.webPreferences {contextIsolation:true, nodeIntegration:false, webviewTag:false, webSecurity:true}` and otherwise `openExternal(url)` or deny (electron.js:2197-2219).

[fact] Engine contracts: WKUIDelegate `webView(_:createWebViewWith:for:windowFeatures:)` 'The web view returned must be created with the specified configuration… A new web view or nil' (R16); WebView2 'If either Handled or NewWindow properties are not set, the target content will be opened on a popup window' (R20) — Keld already installs deny-all (webview2/mod.rs:1936-1946); WebKitGTK `create` 'The new WebKitWebView must be related to web_view… should not be displayed until ready-to-show' (R22).

decisions.question: How does `executeJavaScript` (and WebFrameMain/webFrame variants, insertCSS) return values and errors across three engines without a second IPC path?
decisions.proposed_answer: Extend `WebEngine::eval` (design review) with the destination `EvalCallback` carrying a structured-clone-compatible result or a typed error, implemented by ONE host-owned script envelope: the host wraps `code` as an async IIFE producing `{ok:true,value}` / `{ok:false,name,message,stack}` serialized with a single shared encoder (JSON-with-tags for Date/Map/Set/TypedArray refs → bulk lane per arch 02 §5 SCV codec), evaluated in the PAGE world (`executeJavaScript`) or in a named Keld app world that is never the bridge world (`executeJavaScriptInIsolatedWorld`; world ids are remapped, the KEL-142 world is unreachable). Queue the request until the current generation's did-stop-loading ('suspended until web page stop loading'); a generation rotation before completion rejects with a KELD code (reusing KEL-142 invalidation). `userGesture:true` is ▲ (no engine exposes a user-activation flag for evaluated script; WK/WebView2 may refuse `requestFullscreen`). `insertCSS` returns a host-minted key and is implemented by the same envelope inserting a `<style data-keld-key>`; `removeInsertedCSS` removes it.
evidence: [fact] Electron: 'Returns Promise<any> — resolves with the result of the executed code or is rejected if the result of the code is a rejected promise… Code execution will be suspended until web page stop loading' (R10); WebFrameMain variant 'rejected if execution throws or results in a rejected promise' (R11).
[fact] Corpus: draw.io awaits results at 3+ sites (`collectConfigPathsScript`, recents, settings; electron.js:491, 565, 609) — a `Promise<void>` facade fails draw.io's primary workflow.
[fact] Keld `eval` is fire-and-forget `Result<(), WvError>`; the callback form is explicitly deferred to the command-queue design (engine.rs module doc).

[fact] WebView2 `ExecuteScript`: result 'is a JSON encoded string. If the result is undefined, contains a reference cycle, or otherwise is not able to be encoded into JSON, then the result is considered to be null… If the script that was run throws an unhandled exception, then the result is also "null"' (R20) — undefined/throw/null are indistinguishable without an envelope.

[fact] WebKitGTK `webkit_web_view_evaluate_javascript` (since 2.40) runs in a named script world and returns a JSCValue via `_finish` (R25); WK `evaluateJavaScript(_:in:in:completionHandler:)` is the KEL-142 `evaluate_in_world` path (macos_bridge.rs:797).

decisions.question: What is a 'preload script' in Keld, and what happens to `sandbox:false` / `nodeIntegration:true` apps?
decisions.proposed_answer: A preload is a host-registered, document-start user script in the Keld isolated world (the KEL-142 injection path), main-frame-only by default, bundled by `keld migrate`/`keld build` into the package and resolved by the host from the package root (an absolute path outside the package is a typed refusal, not a filesystem read). The isolated world provides the Electron sandbox `require` polyfill subset ONLY (`events`, `timers`, `url`, `electron` → contextBridge/ipcRenderer/webFrame/nativeImage/webUtils/crashReporter shims over `window.keld`). `sandbox:false` or `nodeIntegration:true` are never honored (no Node in a webview — it is not one of the four uniques, and the strict profile forbids ambient authority): the facade emits an explicit diagnostic and the cell scores ✘ unless `keld migrate`'s static scan proves the preload only uses the sandbox subset, in which case a `keld.compat.ts` quirk (`treatUnsandboxedPreloadAsSandboxed`) lets it run. `preload-error` (path + Error) is emitted when the injected script throws. On WebView2 the injection must use the async completion form (learning: sync form blocks UI 96–109 ms) and must be gated to the main frame (the API injects into all frames).
evidence: [fact] Electron: sandbox 'Default is true since Electron 20'; sandboxed preload `require` is a polyfill limited to events/timers/url + electron subset and 'you will not be able to use CommonJS modules to separate your preload script into multiple files'; 'Sandboxing is also disabled whenever Node.js integration is enabled' (R17, R18); contextIsolation 'enabled by default since Electron 12' (R19); preload 'will always have access to node APIs no matter whether node integration is turned on or off' (R12 — the part Keld cannot and must not clone).

[fact] Corpus: draw.io preload with contextIsolation:true/nodeIntegration:false/webviewTag:false/webSecurity:true (electron.js:721-729) and preload-side isolated-world `navigation` listener; Zettlr: 14 windows with preload, 12 `sandbox:true`, 2 `sandbox:false` (onboarding, splash) with contextIsolation:true.

[fact] KEL-142 §5.1/AC2: isolated `WKContentWorld` scripts at AtDocumentStart; 'page code observes window.keld.invoke before its first script runs'; page world cannot reach the native handler. WebView2 `AddScriptToExecuteOnDocumentCreated` 'runs on all top-level document and child frame page navigations' (R20); 06-webview-reality: pre-load user scripts ✅ on all three engines.

[fact] Electron `webPreferences.nodeIntegrationInSubFrames` default false → preload main-frame-only by default (R12).
